Object Relative Clauses
You use relative clauses to provide extra information about an object.
The problem was that many oscilloscopes were designed for specific purposes, which companies, later on, needed to modify.

In order to create a sentence, we need to use relative pronouns that can replace an object. If a noun or a pronoun is after the relative clause, then it is an object relative clause.

These are the relative pronouns that you can use:

Defining Relative Clauses:
We add important information that is relevant and is that is needed to understand who or what we re referring to.

Examples:
Case studies which experts conducted showed great benefits.
The architecture style that was chosen didn't work.

No-defining Relative Clauses:
In this kind of clauses we don't use the relative pronoun that. The extra information that you want to provide is irrelevant and you have to put it between two commas. This means that the sentence keeps the message with or without the non-defining relative clause.
Look at this sentence:
The case studies had very interesting hypothesis.
Let’s add a non-defining relative clause:
The case studies, which I read, had very interesting hypothesis.
I'm going to outline the stages, which researchers applied, that helped define the correct method.
They tried an object-oriented model, which identified waveforms, to clarify data types.
Another example is:
The architecture style, which I thought would be the best option, ended up being the last option for the case study.
What is a case of study?
A case of study is a record of a real or hypothetical situation used to describe the influences of decisions.
I'm going to present a case of study about instrumentation software and architecture styles. It was written by researchers from Tektronix, Inc. And a computer research laboratory.

Case studies are implemented to describe a behavior of an individual or a group. They are considered a formal research method in many disciplines. The word “case” refers to the situation that is being studied.

There are different types of case studies which could be divided into two main categories; historical and problem orientated. They could be historical where the causes and the consequences of a situation are analyzed so, you are outside the situation. On the other hand, if you want to analyze a current situation and want to find out answers, the case study would be problem orientated as you are part of process.

Some subdivisions of case studies help us identify what we want to accomplish. As an investigator you may want to choose one of the following categories:

Illustrative: These case studies are descriptive. They intend to contextualize readers about an unknown topic.

Exploratory: A case study designed as the first stage before a big investigation. It helps finding questions and possible conclusions.

Cumulative: These studies collect information from other studies in order to obtain generalized concepts.

Critical Instance: Case studies are implemented to analyze cause and effect questions under unique situations.

images.text:
In today's class, I'm going to present a case of study about instrumentation software and architecture styles. It was written by researchers from Tektronix, Inc. in a computer research laboratory. </br>
The study intended to propose a way to develop a reusable system architecture for oscilloscopes, which companies needed to readjust due to changes in hardware capability. The problem was that many oscilloscopes were designed for specific purposes, which companies, later on, needed to modify. Therefore, if they wanted to reuse an item, they had to implement a general-purpose instrument. Another issue was that oscilloscopes weren't programmed within the instrument, so, they had to load a different software every time they needed to cause delays. To solve these problems, they needed to have a domain-specific software architecture.

The first question was, “what architecture style was more appropriate to accomplish what they wanted?” Well, I'm going to outline the stages, which researchers applied, that helped define the correct method. First, they tried an object-oriented model, which identified waveforms, to clarify data types. However, two more questions appeared, “Are measurements associated or represented externally with the type of data?”, and “What objects does the interface user have to talk about?”.  Since all the functions could be defined into groups, these questions were answered by using a layered model. Unfortunately, layers often withstood interaction among functions. Finally, the pipe and filter model suited the expectations after further specialization and development of the style.

If we wanted to summarize this case study, we would say that it took many attempts and deep research to find an appropriate model. One of the main findings was that pipes and filters can be structured for specific needs. Also, any architecture style has to be taken “pure” and then it can be offset depending on the purpose.
